title: infra-sim scenario
description: A scenario file: what happens to a design, and what must hold. (A design can also carry scenarios under scenarios.)

design.description: The design it is for: a path relative to this file (a design, or a template an importer reads), or the design itself.

description.description: What it shows. The first paragraph is its short blurb.

seed.description: Random seed for the run: the same design, scenario and seed always play out the same.

duration.description: How long to run. Required to run it.

warmup.description: Time to let the system settle before measuring: checks and summaries start after it.

scale.description: Multiply every client's request rate: 3 is three times the traffic.

overrides.description: Settings applied at the start, merged over the design's own.

timeline.description: What happens, and when. Each event does one thing; an event with only a note annotates the timeline.

at.description: When it happens, from the start of the run.

note.description: Says what this event is, in the timeline.

target.description: What breaks: node:<id>, edge:<id>, region:<placement> (region:aws:us-east-1) or zone:<placement>:<zone> (zone:aws:us-east-1:us-east-1a).

fault.description: The fault: Outage (Rejects every call at once, like a connection refused or a stopped service. On a region, the whole region is down; on a zone, everything placed in it and every unit a fleet runs there.) Errors (A fraction of calls fail with a server error after being processed.) Slow (Adds fixed latency to every call.) Blackhole (Calls vanish without a reply; callers wait out their full timeout.) Loss (A fraction of calls vanish without a reply.) Crash (Crashes some of a fleet's units at once (EC2 instances, ECS tasks, EKS pods or nodes): calls on them fail, a load balancer keeps sending them traffic until its health checks catch them, and the fleet replaces them when it notices. It happens in an instant; on a component that isn't a fleet it does nothing.) Write it as Outage, Slow(250ms), Errors(20%), Loss(10%), or as an object { type: Slow, extra: 250ms }.

extra.description: A time: a number of seconds, or text such as 90s, 2m, 1h30m, 250ms or "2 minutes".

for.description: How long it lasts. Without it, the fault lasts until cleared.

id.description: A name to clear it by later.

clear.description: Lift a fault by the id it was injected with, or all of them (all).

set.description: Change a node's or an edge's settings while it runs.

settings.description: Settings, merged over what it already has.

account.description: Change the account quotas of a placement while it runs.

settings.description: Settings, merged over what it already has.

assert.description: What must hold. A run passes when every check does.

anyOf.description:
A check that must hold over the run (after the warm-up unless a window is given), in the check language:

<subject>.<metric>[:<aggregate>] <op> <value> [@ <from>..<to>]

subject   a node id; edge:<edge id>; or system (every client together)
metric    errorRatio | successRatio | throughput
          rate.<counter>          per-second rate of a counter: rate.ok, rate.fail, rate.fail.Throttled, rate.in, rate.sent
          total.<counter>         how many events in the window
          gauge.<name>            a gauge: gauge.depth, gauge.concurrent, gauge.inflight, gauge.cacheHitRate
          latency.<stat>          p50 | p95 | p99 | mean | max, of the 'latency' distribution (other distributions: dist.<name>.<stat>)
aggregate how to combine the window's frames: mean (default) | max | min | last | sum
op        < <= > >= == !=
value     a number, with optional unit: 500ms, 2s, 1.5%, 10/s
window    @ 2m..3m measures only that stretch (default: after the warm-up, to the end of the run)

examples  api.errorRatio < 1%
          system.latency.p99 < 800ms
          orders-queue.gauge.depth:max < 5000
          fn.rate.fail.Throttled == 0
          edge:web.out->api.rate.fail < 5/s @ 4m..6m

aggregate how to combine the window's frames: mean (default) | max | min | last | sum
op        < <= > >= == !=
value     a number, with optional unit: 500ms, 2s, 1.5%, 10/s
window    @ 2m..3m measures only that stretch (default: after the warm-up, to the end of the run)

from.description: Measure only from here (default: the end of the warm-up).

to.description: ... to here (default: the end of the run).
